## Problem 1
```{r}
# function that gives each person a random birthday and checks if any two people share one
bday_sim = function(n_room) {
  birthdays = sample(1:365, n_room, replace = TRUE)
  repeated_bday = length(unique(birthdays)) < n_room
  repeated_bday
}
```

```{r}
# runs the function 10,000 times for each group size and averages the results to get the probability
bday_sim_results = 
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    shared_bday = map_lgl(group_size, bday_sim)
  ) |> 
  group_by(group_size) |> 
  summarize(
    prob_shared = mean(shared_bday)
  )
```

```{r}
# plots the probability of a shared birthday by group size
bday_sim_results |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = prob_shared)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_line() + 
  labs(
    title = "Probability of a shared birthday by group size",
    x = "Group size",
    y = "Probability at least two people share a birthday"
  )
```

As the group size increases, the probability of two people sharing a birthday goes up. With small groups the probability is low, but it passes 50% at around 23 people. By 50 people, the probability is close to 1. This is higher than I expected, since 23 people is a lot less than 365 days. It makes sense though, because with more people there are a lot more pairs of people who could share a birthday.
